body:
Source: GitHub issue #981. Re-verified on main @ b378c2a3: plugins/adlc-... N/A; the actual site is packages/fleet/test/git-mirror.test.mjs. Its own `gitAt` helper (line 34-35) is:

```js
const gitAt = (dir) => (...args) =>
  execFileSync('git', ['-c', 'commit.gpgsign=false', ...args], { cwd: dir, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'], env }).trim();
```

It already disables `commit.gpgsign` per-invocation but never touches `gc.auto`/`gc.autoDetach`. Confirmed via grep: neither setting appears anywhere in this test file or in packages/fleet/lib/git-mirror.mjs.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package: packages/fleet. This is the SAME failure class already root-caused and fixed twice in packages/autopilot's own test fixtures (packages/autopilot/test/helpers/recover-fixture.mjs:49-52 and :59-62, packages/autopilot/test/helpers/gates-fixture.mjs:46, packages/autopilot/test/helpers/preflight-ctx.mjs:92) with the identical inline comment pattern: "a background gc keeps writing into repo/.git after the last git command returns, racing the teardown's recursive rm (CI ENOTEMPTY flake, 2026-08-31/2026-08-30)". Every one of those fixes is the same two-line addition: `git config gc.auto 0` and `git config gc.autoDetach false` on every git directory the fixture creates, immediately after `git init`/`git clone --bare`. packages/fleet/test/git-mirror.test.mjs's `makeFixture()` (line 59-83) creates a working repo via `g('init', ...)` and a bare mirror via `gitAt(root)('clone', '-q', '--bare', ...)` — NEITHER gets this protection.

The test's own `cleanup` is `() => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true })` (line 82) — no `maxRetries`/`retryDelay`, unlike autopilot's fixture (`cleanup: () => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 10, retryDelay: 50 })`). Consider whether the retry budget is also worth adding here as defense-in-depth, but the PRIMARY fix (matching every prior instance of this exact bug class in this repo) is disabling auto-gc so there is nothing racing the rm in the first place.

Tests: `node --test packages/fleet/test/git-mirror.test.mjs` from the worktree root. This is the ONLY test file that needs a change — the fix is entirely inside its own `gitAt` helper and/or `makeFixture()`.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. In `makeFixture()`, immediately after `g('init', '-q', '-b', 'main')` (line 64) and immediately after the bare clone (`gitAt(root)('clone', ...)`, line 78), set `gc.auto=0` and `gc.autoDetach=false` on that repository — either via two extra `g(...)`/`gitAt(mirror)(...)` config calls (matching autopilot's `sh(['config', 'gc.auto', '0']); sh(['config', 'gc.autoDetach', 'false']);` pattern) or by adding `-c gc.auto=0 -c gc.autoDetach=false` to the shared `gitAt` helper's argv so every invocation carries it (simpler, and this test file's `gitAt` is used for EVERY git call across every test in the file — verify neither approach breaks a test that asserts on `git config --list` output, e.g. the test at line 100 `assert.doesNotMatch(gitAt(f.mirror)('config', '--list', '--local'), /^remote\./m, ...)` — a per-call `-c` flag does NOT persist into the repo's on-disk config and so will NOT show up in `config --list --local`, unlike an explicit `git config` write; prefer the per-call `-c` flag approach for exactly this reason, since it protects every fixture without adding a new persisted config line that other assertions might trip over).
2. Do not change `packages/fleet/lib/git-mirror.mjs` (production code) — this ticket is about the TEST fixture's flakiness only. Production `defaultGit` does not create the ad-hoc fixtures that raced; if a maintainer later decides production callers need the same protection, that is a separate, deliberate decision outside this ticket's scope.
3. Add a short comment at the fix site (matching the existing convention in autopilot's fixtures) explaining WHY: background auto-gc can hold `.git` files open after the parent git command returns, racing the test's teardown `rmSync`.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 `makeFixture()`'s working repo and bare mirror are both created with `gc.auto=0` and `gc.autoDetach=false` in effect for every subsequent git command run against them. verify: `node --test packages/fleet/test/git-mirror.test.mjs` — add a new assertion (in a NEW test, not modifying an existing one) that reads back the effective config (e.g. `gitAt(f.repo)('config', 'gc.auto')` returns `'0'`, or if using the per-call `-c` flag approach, assert the flag is present in the `gitAt` helper's own argv construction — whichever mechanism is chosen, the AC must assert the MECHANISM is actually wired, not just assume it from reading the diff).
- AC2 Existing suite green, including the config-list assertion at line ~100 that must NOT see a new persisted `gc.` line if the per-call `-c` approach is used. verify: `node --test packages/fleet/test/git-mirror.test.mjs`
- AC3 Full package suite green. verify: `node scripts/run-tests.mjs fleet` (or `node --test packages/fleet/test/*.test.mjs` if run-tests.mjs is unavailable in the worktree)
- AC4 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: packages/fleet/lib/git-mirror.mjs (production code, per NORMATIVE #2). Any OTHER fleet test file's fixture helpers — this ticket is scoped to git-mirror.test.mjs specifically, the file cited in issue #981. Adding a retry budget to `cleanup()` is optional defense-in-depth, not required for AC pass, if the gc.auto fix alone resolves the loop-reproduction (loop `node --test packages/fleet/test/git-mirror.test.mjs` at least 50 times locally before and after the fix to build confidence, though CI cannot verify a flake's absence directly — the AC1 mechanism assertion is the durable proof).
title: fleet: disable git-mirror test fixture's background auto-gc to fix the ENOTEMPTY teardown flake
